children: Enterprise software provider's Q1 revenue up 30% yr/yr, slightly beating analyst expectations
Adjusted EPS for Q1 rose 30% and beat analyst expectations
Remaining performance obligations jump to $664 billion after $30 billion in new AI cloud contracts
Company completed $20 bln stock sale via ATM equity program as part of capital investment plan
Shares of the company were up about 7% after the bell
Oracle expects Q2 revenue to grow 30%-34% in constant currency and USD
Company sees Q2 cloud revenue up 64%-70% in constant currency, 65%-71% in USD
Oracle forecasts FY27 revenue of at least $90 bln and non-GAAP EPS of $8.10
CLOUD INFRASTRUCTURE DEMAND - Q1 cloud infrastructure (IaaS) revenue rose 121% yr/yr, driven by strong customer demand, especially for AI cloud training and inferencing services
DATACENTER EXPANSION - Co delivered 850MW additional datacenter capacity and nearly tripled GPU deliveries since Q4 FY26 to support cloud growth
ON-PREMISES SOFTWARE MIGRATION - Software revenues fell 3% as customers continued shifting from on-premises software to cloud offerings
*Applies to a deviation of less than 1%; not applicable for per-share numbers.
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "buy" and the breakdown of recommendations is 34 "strong buy" or "buy", 7 "hold" and 1 "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the software peer group is "buy"
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Oracle Corporation is $245.00, about 51.6% above its September 9 closing price of $161.63
The stock recently traded at 18 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 28 three months ago
